Question: In the trypan blue staining, 25 % of the cells are blue. What does that mean?

Options:
A. that 25 % of the cells are dead
B. that 75 % of the cells are dead
C. that all cells are alive, but the cell membrane is partially penetrated by trypan blue
D. that the mitochondria of the cell only perform at 25 %

Thought: Trypan blue is a dye used in cell biology to selectively color dead cells. The principle behind this staining is that live cells have intact cell membranes that exclude trypan blue, while dead cells have compromised membranes that allow the dye to enter, thus staining them blue. Therefore, if 25% of the cells are blue in a trypan blue staining, it indicates that 25% of the cells are dead.
